Use case: illustration-story. Generate ONE standalone 16:9 horizontal Chinese article BODY illustration, ideally 1280x720. Pure #FFFFFF background, no transparency. Minimal black hand-drawn line art with lightly wobbly thin pen strokes; flat red/orange/blue sparingly, huge white negative space (at least 40%). Clean absurd adult product sketch, not a formal infographic. No title, no corner heading, no frame, no panels, no gradients, shadows, paper texture, dense screens, charts, benchmark numbers, watermarks, commercial vector polish, PPT styling, or cute children's cartoon.
The recurring protagonist XiaoM 小M is a small serious deadpan mushroom worker: flat RED dome cap with 3–5 WHITE polka dots and thin irregular black contour; pale cream stem body, two tiny BLACK dot eyes, thin stick arms and legs, no smile or clothes. NOT a solid black mushroom. XiaoM performs the central conceptual action. Orange means movement; blue means supplementary state; black main drawing. Tiny Chinese handwritten annotations only where specified; do not add explanatory paragraphs. Keep all elements inside generous margins.
Scene: a physical change-notification desk, drawn as an airy single hand-drawn scene. A modest hanging desk bell at left is rung by an arriving structured field-change card; tiny blue sound marks. The card has only two short rows labeled “对象” and “变化”, with a small orange change mark, no dense data. At center XiaoM actively receives this card with one hand and compares it to a small separate action-result slip marked “结果” with the other, seriously checking object identity and action outcome rather than blindly acting. A very small magnifying glass sits on a side hook within reach, its lens showing a simple picture thumbnail (one mountain), no detailed UI. It is available for optional visual inspection, visibly intact and never crossed out. The structured cards dominate the workflow; the visual magnifier is secondary and small. A short faint blue dotted reach from XiaoM to magnifier conveys optional use.
Only exact Chinese labels: “变化通知” by bell, “对象” and “变化” on incoming card, “结果” on held slip, “按需看图” beside small magnifier. No other text. The core meaning is structured changes summon the agent; it checks object/action results and still has vision when needed, NOT elimination of vision. Aim for a distinctive quiet desk-bell metaphor, 3 principal object groups spread through center of white canvas.

Scene: ONE shared identity keyring supplying TWO separate Session workbenches. One single large ordinary keyring hangs above the center, attached to a SINGLE identity tag reading “Computer”. Directly below tag a short blue handwritten note reads “同一登录”. The keyring contains a pair of ordinary small keys, NOT two separate identity badges. Exactly TWO thin orange branching cords connect this ONE keyring to two low separate workbenches on left and right. Each bench holds its own simple open browser WINDOW outline (not a screen full of data) and its own small file tray with a sheet. Browser windows have the SAME tiny blue circular account mark to reinforce the SAME tenant login. The windows and paper files are visibly physically separate, not merged.
ONE XiaoM worker centrally spans the gap, actively adjusting the left browser window with one extended arm while placing a separate paper file onto the right workbench with its other arm. Feet between desks, serious posture. Left bench small label “Session A”; right bench “Session B”. A small unobtrusive blue shared annotation below the two benches reads “窗口、文件分开”. Draw as a funny physical workshop, not architecture boxes or a rigid flowchart.
Only text: “Computer”, “同一登录”, “Session A”, “Session B”, “窗口、文件分开”. No security shields, padlocks, barriers, walls, separate users, separate passwords, separate tenants or isolation claim. Separation concerns workspaces only; identity and login are shared. Keep enormous white space.

Scene: a sparse hand-drawn closeout tabletop for a recoverable agent job. Single integrated wide scene, no panels. At left a durable request-token card is visibly secured in a small archival clip anchored to a tabletop, label “存好请求键”. A thin orange loop goes from this SAME clipped token to ONE small task spool and back: a tiny torn return envelope on the loop, label “回执丢失”; beside the intact return path write “同键恢复”. Show only ONE job spool, never two duplicate jobs, and no second new token. The loop means request-level recovery, not repeated external business actions.
At center XiaoM actively inspects an EXTERNAL business receipt (tiny shop-roof symbol on receipt, a blank row with check mark), with a small hand-held magnifier in one hand; nearby short label “核对业务”. With its other hand it places an exported artifact sheet into its OWN open storage chest on the right, clearly labeled “自有存储”. A small orange motion line leads the file INTO this chest. The chest, not the remote runtime, owns the artifact. Beyond the chest at far right is a small simple power toggle with label “再停止”, separated by a little breathing space. Crucial visual ordering left to right: persist token / same-job recovery, check external business outcome, export and store file in own chest, only then reach power toggle. XiaoM is busy checking and archiving; toggle still untouched.
Small restrained red handwritten caution under the request loop ONLY: “去重≠恰好一次”. This caution means run idempotency is NOT exactly-once remote website actions. Do not imply the checkmark or request token automatically proves external success. No automatic repeated payment, email, order actions. All labels exactly these seven: “存好请求键”, “回执丢失”, “同键恢复”, “核对业务”, “自有存储”, “再停止”, “去重≠恰好一次”. No other text, no numbers. Keep objects simple and compact, abundant blank white above and below.
